# File system

Deleting, copying and moving files, directories, attributes, search and links.

<h2 id="file-attribute-readonly"><code>FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY: uint32 = 0x00000001;
```

`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY`: the file may not be opened for writing or deleted.
The whole of Windows' permission model as this package uses it: there are ACLs underneath, but nothing in the
portable surface can express them, and this bit is what `chmod` maps onto.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L55)

<h2 id="file-attribute-directory"><code>FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY: uint32 = 0x00000010;
```

`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY`: the name is a directory.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L60)

<h2 id="file-attribute-reparse-point"><code>FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT: uint32 = 0x00000400;
```

`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT`: the name carries a reparse point, which is what a symbolic link is.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L65)

<h2 id="invalid-file-attributes"><code>INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES</code></h2>

```rux
pub const INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES: uint32 = 0xFFFFFFFF;
```

`INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES`: what [`GetFileAttributesW`](/docs/api/windows/file-system#get-file-attributes-w) returns when it could not answer.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L70)

<h2 id="symbolic-link-flag-directory"><code>SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_DIRECTORY</code></h2>

```rux
pub const SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_DIRECTORY: uint32 = 0x00000001;
```

`SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_DIRECTORY`: the link's target is a directory.
Windows types its symbolic links: a link made without this flag misbehaves when its target is a directory,
which no Unix symlink ever asked anyone to know in advance.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L98)

<h2 id="symbolic-link-flag-allow-unprivileged-create"><code>SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_ALLOW_UNPRIVILEGED_CREATE</code></h2>

```rux
pub const SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_ALLOW_UNPRIVILEGED_CREATE: uint32 = 0x00000002;
```

`SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_ALLOW_UNPRIVILEGED_CREATE`: let a Developer Mode machine create the link without the
privilege older systems demand.
Harmless where the privilege is held; without Developer Mode or the privilege the call still fails with
[`ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD`](/docs/api/windows/errors#error-privilege-not-held).

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L106)

<h2 id="move-file-replace-existing"><code>MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING</code></h2>

```rux
pub const MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING: uint32 = 0x00000001;
```

`MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING`: let the move overwrite an existing target.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L111)

<h2 id="move-file-write-through"><code>MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH</code></h2>

```rux
pub const MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH: uint32 = 0x00000008;
```

`MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH`: do not return until the move has reached the disk.
With [`MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING`](/docs/api/windows/file-system#move-file-replace-existing), this is what makes publishing a file under its final name durable.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L117)

<h2 id="find-first-file-w"><code>FindFirstFileW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func FindFirstFileW(
    fileName: *char16,
    findFileData: *var opaque
) -> *var opaque
```

Begins a directory enumeration matching a UTF-16 pattern.
Returns InvalidHandleValue on failure. `findFileData` receives a WIN32_FIND_DATAW record: attributes at
offset 0 (4 bytes), three FILETIMEs from 4, the size's halves at 28 and 32, and the entry's NUL-terminated
UTF-16 name from offset 44. The record is 592 bytes.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-findfirstfilew](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-findfirstfilew)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L146)

**Parameters**

| Name           | Type          | Description                           |
| -------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `fileName`     | `*char16`     | the path, as a null-terminated string |
| `findFileData` | `*var opaque` | receives the entry's record           |

**Returns**: a search handle, or [`InvalidHandleValue`](/docs/api/windows/types#invalid-handle-value)

<h2 id="create-symbolic-link-w"><code>CreateSymbolicLinkW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func CreateSymbolicLinkW(
    symlinkFileName: *char16,
    targetFileName: *char16,
    flags: uint32
) -> uint8
```

Creates a symbolic link; returns a BOOLEAN, so only the low byte is meaningful.
Creation needs SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege or a Developer Mode machine with the allow-unprivileged flag;
without either it fails with ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-createsymboliclinkw](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-createsymboliclinkw)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L174)

**Parameters**

| Name              | Type      | Description                              |
| ----------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `symlinkFileName` | `*char16` | the link to create                       |
| `targetFileName`  | `*char16` | the path the link will point at          |
| `flags`           | `uint32`  | the call's flag bits, combined with `\|` |

**Returns**: non-zero on success; creating one needs a privilege or developer mode

<h2 id="get-temp-path-w"><code>GetTempPathW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GetTempPathW(
    bufferLength: uint32,
    buffer: *var char16
) -> uint32
```

Writes the path of the directory designated for temporary files.
Returns the length written without the terminator, or the required length when the buffer is too small, or
zero on failure. The answer always ends in a backslash. Consults TMP, then TEMP, then USERPROFILE, then the
Windows directory, so it answers even where none of those are set.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-gettemppathw](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-gettemppathw)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L222)

**Parameters**

| Name           | Type          | Description                   |
| -------------- | ------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `bufferLength` | `uint32`      | how many units `buffer` holds |
| `buffer`       | `*var char16` | the bytes                     |

**Returns**: the length written including the separator, or zero on failure

<h2 id="move-file-ex-w"><code>MoveFileExW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func MoveFileExW(
    existingFileName: *char16,
    newFileName: *char16,
    flags: uint32
) -> int32
```

Moves or renames a file or directory, taking UTF-16 paths.
With MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING this replaces the target atomically within a volume, which is how a file is
published under its final name. Across volumes it copies and deletes instead, which is not atomic.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-movefileexw](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-movefileexw)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L240)

**Parameters**

| Name               | Type      | Description                              |
| ------------------ | --------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `existingFileName` | `*char16` | the path that exists now                 |
| `newFileName`      | `*char16` | the path it should have afterwards       |
| `flags`            | `uint32`  | the call's flag bits, combined with `\|` |

**Returns**: non-zero on success

<h2 id="move-file-a"><code>MoveFileA</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func MoveFileA(
    existingFileName: *char8,
    newFileName: *char8
) -> bool32
```

Moves an existing file or directory.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-movefilea](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-movefilea)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Kernel.rux#L283)

**Parameters**

| Name               | Type     | Description                        |
| ------------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `existingFileName` | `*char8` | the path that exists now           |
| `newFileName`      | `*char8` | the path it should have afterwards |

**Returns**: non-zero on success, and zero on failure with the reason in [`GetLastError`](/docs/api/windows/errors#get-last-error)
